status: Nested Windows result-path defect reproduced in unchanged prior package and fixed; exact corrected Windows package validated; unreleased development candidate

userEvidence.privacy: User account/directory paths and raw uploaded files are intentionally not committed.
userEvidence.orchestratorFailure: Declared SAM output reported missing; downstream steps blocked.
userEvidence.systemLongPathsSetting: Not included in user report; no claim about user registry configuration.

diagnosis: Native runner successfully created and hashed the output. Python orchestration used an ordinary-path existence check on a 269-character path, beyond the legacy Windows boundary. The native runner already uses extended-length file I/O; Python pipeline I/O needs the same handling.
validationGap: Prior candidate used ordinary/space-containing paths that did not establish legacy-limit behavior for deep pipeline results. Its successful evidence remains valid only within that scope.
limits: No universal long-path support claim for every optional pack, arbitrary deep installations or Windows shell dialogs.
Raw user data retained only in the authorized attachment/workspace, not uploaded to the repository.
Long-path gate used a short installation root, a 152-character synthetic output parent, a native working directory below 260, and output files up to 279 characters.
New long-path check uses the actual private host Check installation action; it does not claim long-path GUI interaction.
Existing GUI evidence remains Windows Server 2022 at 96 DPI; physical trackpad pinch, high-DPI, multi-monitor and folder-picker behavior and manual acceptance remain unvalidated.
No 0.8.0 release published; candidate updater tested only from 0.6.0; no 0.7.0 upgrade pass claimed.
diagnosisConfirmed: Exact previous package reproduced the false missing-SAM error under disabled long-path policy. The corrected package completed all five scientific steps under the same policy, while ordinary unprefixed is_file still returned false for the 268-character SAM.
implementation: Reuse existing extended Windows filesystem paths at engine I/O boundaries; retain ordinary serialized paths and tool arguments.
Cover output detection, hashing, upstream reads, preflight readers, reports, cancellation and run records.
Use the same physical I/O boundary for starter/pack scientific output assertions.
Preserve exact pack bytes, frozen plan/manifest validation, containment and link/file identity protections.

sourceChecks.newPathTestsScope: Linux real files with emulated MAX_PATH and synthetic backend; not native Windows evidence.

additionalLocalChecks.scope: Selected source contracts on Python 3.12.14; the separate portable Linux scientific integration test was not run. Full actual Windows scientific chain is covered below.
